name: weakness overview
title: Weakness: upper motor neuron signs place the lesion in the brain or spinal cord, lower motor neuron signs in the root, nerve, neuromuscular junction or muscle; the pattern of weakness and its companions localize it, and the tempo of onset gives the differential

root.title: WEAKNESS: WHERE is the lesion, and how FAST did it come?
lines: describe → LOCALIZE (upper or lower motor neuron, then the pattern) → differential by TEMPO → plan tests
cerebellum and basal ganglia do NOT cause weakness: incoordination, parkinsonism or extra movements instead

groups.title: UPPER motor neuron (UMN): CENTRAL
lines: brisk reflexes · Babinski (extensor plantar) · spasticity · NO atrophy, NO fasciculations

groups.title: LOWER motor neuron (LMN): PERIPHERAL
lines: reflexes ↓ or absent · plantar flexor or absent · normal tone · ATROPHY · fasciculations possible

head: h
Spinal cord
• hemibody, face SPARED
• 4 limbs: cervical
• both legs: thoracic (or lumbar roots)
clue: NO head CT for a cord problem

rows: Then the TEMPO of onset gives the differential
• HYPERACUTE, seconds to minutes: STROKE until proven otherwise · migraine aura (resolves in minutes) · trauma
• ACUTE, hours to a couple of days: inflammation, infection
• SUBACUTE, days to weeks: inflammation, infection, tumour, toxic
• CHRONIC, months to years: degenerative, hereditary
